name: Berkeley fully depleted back-illuminated CCD
description: Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory developed a thick back-illuminated CCD on high-resistivity silicon. Full depletion of the thick substrate increased the response to red and near-infrared light and allowed operation without thinning the silicon to improve blue response.

date.basis: Date of the field test reported by the observing team.

events.statement: A back-illuminated Berkeley CCD imaged part of the Orion Nebula on the Lick Observatory's 1 m Nickel telescope.

evidence.supports: The observing team names the date, telescope, prototype and two test images.

date.basis: Conference proceedings attribution, corroborated by Holland's 2006 SNIC presentation. The prototype's fabrication preceded publication.

events.statement: The Berkeley team and Lick Observatory collaborators reported a 200 × 200 test CCD operated with its 300 μm silicon substrate fully depleted and demonstrated backside illumination.

evidence.locator: PostScript p. 1, abstract and §§1–2; p. 4, conclusions
evidence.supports: The 1996 paper reports a fabricated, fully depleted 200 × 200 sensor and successful backside illumination.

events.statement: A Lick Observatory-led paper reported characterization of the Berkeley CCD and described astronomical observations with a back-illuminated sample at the Lick 1 m reflector.

evidence.supports: The authors report measurements on the prototype, its limitations and astronomical observations with the prototype at Lick.

earliest_record.rationale: The exact-dated telescope test documents operation in December 1996. The conference paper establishes an earlier laboratory prototype without an exact fabrication date.

links.statement: Did the specific high-resistivity silicon fabrication process documented in the 1988 preprint and 1989 article provide the CCD's backside-gettering approach?
links.finding: The 1996 prototype paper credits earlier p-i-n detector work and cites the 1989 article. The 1997 paper repeats this attribution with overlapping authorship. Independent corroboration identifying the specific process remains open.

evidence.supports: The CCD developers state that the new CCD was based on fully depleted p-i-n research and cite the specific 1989 fabrication study; the CCD uses backside gettering.
The Lick characterization traces the CCD to Berkeley p-i-n work, identifies backside gettering in the device, and separately cites the same 1989 fabrication article.

links.statement: The Berkeley detector retains the charge-coupled principle of collecting and moving packets of charge under clocked electrodes.
links.caveats: The evidence compares the operating principle. The route by which the Berkeley team took up the early CCD design is unresolved.

evidence.supports: The Bell Labs paper describes charge storage and clocked transfer between potential wells.
The prototype transfers collected charge under clocked drive; the paper measures its charge-transfer performance.

why: The prototype addressed weak red and near-infrared response and interference fringes in thinned scientific CCDs, while using back illumination for short-wavelength response.
